findings.reason: narrowing as a *replacement* for the enforced guard has no precedent in this apply, so the "concurrency argument" in §2 supports adding a narrow instrument beside the guard, not replacing it, and the measurement plan should say which it is testing.
findings.text: the plan's §2 precedent overstates the case: the 1,411-row "external non-cohort HAS_PARENT" digest that stayed at ea87d5dc was an *external collateral instrument* (a supplementary proof), and the same document states "The signed executor also enforced its own out-of-allowlist closure inside the transaction" — i.e. the graph-wide `_collateral_snapshot` remained the enforced guard while the narrowing applied only to the extra instrument

findings.reason: the plan should reuse or cite this owner rather than present narrowing as novel, and its open question (derive vs hand-declare owned dimensions) already has a worked answer there.
findings.text: census of existing narrow-collateral owners the plan does not cite: `release_stranded_refine_claim` computes a per-operation `collateral_proof` (`node_properties_except_release_fields_unchanged`, `relationships_unchanged`, `source_bindings_...)`, `source_projections_unchanged`, `lineage_unchanged`) and refuses on drift with a test that mutates collateral and asserts rollback — this is the exactly-owned-dimension design §2 calls the second candidate fix

findings.reason: the plan should derive owned dimensions from the participant `graph_label` set already present, rather than add a parallel declaration, which removes the open question in §2 and shrinks the change.
findings.text: the "narrow to owned" option would fork the operation-owned dimension set the authority already declares: each participant carries `participant["graph_label"]` (:2214), constrained to `_NODE_LABELS`/`_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES` (:1220-1226), and each mutation names its `participant_id`; `_build_preview` already reduces that to `admitted_node_ids`/`admitted_relationship_ids` (:3619-3634) — a new hand-declared "owned dimensions" field would duplicate this and could be mis-set, which is exactly what the authority validation exists to prevent

findings.reason: the plan's scope should name the three call sites; otherwise the implementation node discovers a broader blast radius than the deliverables describe.
findings.text: `_collateral_snapshot` has three call sites with divergent exclusion sets and the plan treats it as one owner: the stale-source adapter preview (:3510, `node_ids`/`relationship_ids` over stale actions, :3487-3502), the ordinary preview (:3635) and the apply verification (:7878); a signature change to carry "owned dimensions" touches the stale-source and error-sibling adapter paths (:3519-3521 dispatch) as well as the two build paths, which §3 does not name

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; it modifies one existing function, so there is no new interface to judge smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the "narrow to the dimensions the operation owns" option treats owned-dimension derivation as unsolved, but the operation already declares its owned dimensions per participant (`participant["graph_label"]`, signed_manifest.py:2221, validated against the same two frozensets at :1220-1226) and `_build_preview` already computes the owned id sets it uses as exclusions (`admitted_node_ids`/`admitted_relationship_ids`, :3619-3634); the owner to extend is `_collateral_snapshot`'s existing `excluded_node_ids`/`excluded_relationship_ids` parameterization, not a parallel declaration.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan adds no CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family, so no section adds interface surface that would need to name a retirement or a merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites one precedent (the relocation-retirement apply, "1,411 rows") but does not cite the existing narrow-collateral owner `release_stranded_refine_claim` (graph_ops.py:24170, its `collateral_proof` at graph_ops.py:24341, tested at tests/standard_names/test_refine_claim_recovery.py:205 and :291), which already implements the "cover only the dimensions the operation owns" shape, nor the five-key per-operation projection it emits.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no thin layer over existing machinery is proposed; both candidate fixes change the existing function in place rather than wrapping it.
